LESSON: MOMENTS AND EQUILIBRIUM

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: PHYSICS FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Mechanics and Thermal Physics
Topic 1.5: Moments and equilibrium
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Moments and equilibrium, part of Mechanics and Thermal Physics in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 PHYSICS FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How does the stability of bodies affect the designs of their structures?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Moments and equilibrium together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and Imaginations: The learner develops observation skills as they discover fresh ways of doing things

while carrying out activities to demonstrate torque and couple.

• Citizenship: the learner develops active community life skills as they show responsibility to the community while

carrying out activities to investigate the factors that affect stability of objects.

Values ;

• Unity: as the learner shows fairness by displaying team spirit while designing and carrying out activities to determine

the position of centre of gravity of regular and irregular objects.

• Integrity: the learner practices virtue of honesty while presenting genuine results as they design and carry out activities

to determine the position of centre of gravity of regular and irregular objects.
